item.title: Time your server in one line.
item.description:
30-second trick: Time your server in one line.
curl can report when the first byte of the page arrived. web.dev suggests a Time to First Byte of 0.8 seconds or less for most sites.
Try it now: Run it a few times on your home page and your slowest template. Over 0.8 seconds? Look at the server before the front end.
How a public-page review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=evergreen-2026-11&utm_content=ttfb-curl
#WebPerformance #Playwright #QA #TTFB #DevTools #QAlab

item.title: Myth: a Lighthouse 100 means accessible.
item.description:
Myth vs fact: Myth: a Lighthouse 100 means accessible.
Lighthouse checks what software can detect, such as names, contrast and ARIA. It cannot tell whether alt text makes sense or whether a screen reader user can finish the task.
Check it: After the score, try one real task with a screen reader: VoiceOver on a Mac, NVDA on Windows.
How a public-page review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=evergreen-2026-11&utm_content=myth-lighthouse

item.title: Valle del Cauca locks the pinch-zoom.
item.description:
HSTS runs a full year, framing is limited, and cookies are Secure. But the viewport tag says user-scalable=no, so people who need larger text cannot pinch to zoom on a phone.
The lesson for every team: Drop user-scalable=no and maximum-scale from the viewport tag, so people can zoom to at least 200%.
